Moving one entry leaves that image, and no mask coefficients reproduce it.  The round is named by re-solving with each round's equations dropped in turn

at_an_a_row.where_it_fires: NOT on the a-row itself: the a-rows carry Q = 256 pads against 252 distinct sampled nodes, so their Cauchy block is square and nonsingular and the pads absorb the moved target exactly.  It fires on the FOUR rows below -- b_re, b_im, u_re, u_im, at that one column and at no other -- because b is the residue of q and u the residue of the proximity vector: absorbing the move on the a-row moves the verifier's per-column identity at that node, and the capture's own b and u entries there contradict it.  The pads buy the a-row and pay for it four rows down

M2_one_opened_column_entry_moved.why: the b and u rows are not free: b is forced by q and u by the proximity vector, so their column values are determined once the a-rows are.  A moved entry on one of them cannot be met, and a moved entry on an a-row cannot be met either -- it reappears on them

M3_declared_functional_order_permuted.what: functionals 0 and 1 of the DECLARED order swapped, so each takes the other's power of theta
M3_declared_functional_order_permuted.why: the first flavour fails b's zero sum: the permuted batch is a different functional of the same coefficients.  The second removes that excuse by forcing the coefficients onto the PERMUTED plane -- b is then admissible and the view STILL has no preimage, because the verifier's per-column identity acc = sum_s a_s(x) W_s(x) + b(x) reads the weights themselves.
